title: Kinetic Analysis of HDAC and Sirtuin Mediated Deacylation on Histones and Nucleosomes
author: Niu, Zhang, et al.

steps.title: Prepare enzymes and substrates
steps.instruction: Purify class I HDAC complexes from mammalian cells (≈1‑10 µM stock) or express tag‑free full‑length SIRT enzymes in bacteria (10‑100 µM stock). Generate full‑length free histone proteins (H3 or H2B) or nucleosome core particles (NCPs) by total/semi‑synthesis or chemoenzymatic synthesis, ensuring the final substrate concentration is ≥5 µM. Include any required cofactors (e.g., NAD stock solution) and inhibitors/activators (MS‑275, IRBM6, MDL‑800 (Sigma cat. no. SML2529‑5MG), CL‑5D) dissolved in DMSO (Sigma cat. no. D4540) as needed.

steps.title: Aliquot and store reagents
steps.instruction: Aliquot HDAC complexes, SIRT enzymes, and NCP substrates into low‑binding tubes containing 5‑20 % glycerol, flash‑freeze, and store at –80 °C. Keep NCPs at concentrations above 5 µM, avoid freeze‑thaw cycles, and use each aliquot within 1 week. After thawing, use HDAC aliquots within 2 days; prolonged storage at –80 °C reduces activity.

steps.title: Quench reaction samples
steps.instruction: At each desired time point, add an equal volume of dual‑quench (DQ) buffer (2× Laemmli sample buffer supplemented with 20 mM EDTA) to the reaction. This yields a final concentration of 10 mM EDTA and 1× Laemmli buffer, instantly terminating HDAC or SIRT activity.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE and Western blot
steps.instruction: Load quenched samples onto SDS‑PAGE gels, perform electrophoresis, transfer proteins to a membrane, and probe with site‑specific anti‑acetyl/acyl‑lysine antibodies (and a total histone antibody as loading control, e.g., anti‑H3, Abcam cat. no. ab1791). Detect signals using chemiluminescence on a suitable imaging system (e.g., Bio‑Rad ChemiDoc).

steps.title: Quantify band intensity
steps.instruction: Use ImageJ to measure band intensities. Normalize to the time‑0 signal (and to the corresponding total‑histone band if required). Fit the normalized data to a first‑order decay curve (Y₀ = 1, plateau = 0, K > 0) to obtain the kinetic parameter V/[E] ± SEM. For multiple enzyme concentrations, compare V/[E] values within the linear range. For Michaelis‑Menten analysis, fit V/[E] versus NCP concentration to determine K_M(NCP) and (V/[E])_max(NCP). For activator titrations, fit dose‑response curves (log[activator] vs response, four‑parameter variable‑slope model) to calculate EC₅₀.
